newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent firms as Nigerian output cut deepens.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent firms as Nigerian output cut deepens.

text.p: IPE Brent crudes futures edged higher on Thursday morning despite a weaker opening call, on news of possible disruptions to Nigerian crude exports, brokers said.
May Brent was trading 14 cents higher at $19.43 a barrel at 1114 GMT.
"We saw long liquidation last night but now people want to think about whether they want to go short into the weekend with this Nigerian situation," said one broker.

Shell said on Thursday that a seventh oil installation on the Niger Delta was occupied last Saturday by local villagers, forcing the oil giant to cut back production by a total of 210,000 barrels per day (bpd).
A senior official at Nigeria National Petroleum Corporation said that Shell could declare force majeure on early April cargoes.
May Brent shed early gains on Wednesday to close 26 cents down at $19.20 a barrel.
"It was all doom and gloom after last night's close, technically it was very poor," said one broker. "But the (Nigerian) headlines are turning it around."
Brokers pegged resistance at the 13-day moving average around $19.65 a barrel.
April gas oil was trading $2.75 a tonne lower at $169.75, as the contract caught up with the 60-cent losses made by Brent after gas oil ceased trading on Wednesday.
